deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1953 drafting of a section on exterior powers of Hilbert spaces. It is preparatory material for a Fredholm theory in Banach and Hilbert spaces, where the Fredholm determinant is controlled through norms on \hat\Lambda^n E. Earlier chapters ('Chap I, §1, N°1', 'Chap I, §2, N°2') are cited.

Setting: E is a (complex) Hilbert space. On \Lambda^n E there is a unique positive definite Hermitian form satisfying the Gram formula (4): (a_1∧…∧a_n, b_1∧…∧b_n) = det((a_i,b_j)). The completion is the Hilbert space \hat\Lambda^n E.

Pasted slip (a correction glued over the page):
- Let (e_i)_{i∈I} be an orthonormal (Hilbert) basis of E.
- For each increasing n-tuple J = (i_1<…<i_n), set e_J = e_{i_1}∧…∧e_{i_n}.
- By (4), (e_J, e_{J'}) = δ_{J,J'}, because the Gram matrix is a permutation-free 0/1 matrix.
- Completeness: the linear span of the e_J equals the span of the image of E_0^n under the natural multilinear map E^n → \Lambda E. Here E_0 is the algebraic span of the e_i.
- E_0 is dense in E and the multilinear map is continuous (by (5)/Hadamard). So this span is dense in \hat\Lambda^n E, and the e_J form a Hilbert basis.

Main text, proof of the norm inequality ||a_1∧…∧a_n|| = det((a_i,a_j))^{1/2} ≤ ∏||a_i||:
- Reduce to the span of the a_i and choose an orthonormal basis there. Write a_i = Σ_j a_ij e_j and A = (a_ij).
- Then (a_i,a_j) = Σ_k a_ik \overline{a_jk} = (AA*)_{ij}, so det((a_i,a_j)) = |det A|^2.
- Hadamard's inequality |det A| ≤ ∏||a_i|| is the statement that the volume of the parallelepiped on the a_i is at most the product of its edge lengths.
- It is proved by choosing the basis (Gram–Schmidt adapted to the flag of the a_i) so that A is triangular. Then det A = ∏ a_ii and |a_ii| ≤ ||a_i||.

Corollary: |det((a_i,b_j))| ≤ ∏||a_i|| ||b_i||. This is Cauchy–Schwarz in \hat\Lambda^n E combined with the norm inequality.

The next page goes on to show that for operators ||u_1∧…∧u_n|| ≤ ∏||u_i||. The point is that the constants appearing in the general Banach-space theory of Chap. I can be taken equal to 1 for Hilbert spaces. This is the kind of estimate needed for Fredholm determinants, det(1+u) = Σ tr Λ^n u.
errors: No mathematical errors. Two small gaps: the reduction to the finite-dimensional span of the a_i is implicit, and the claim that one can choose the orthonormal basis so that A is triangular (Gram–Schmidt along the flag span(a_1) ⊂ span(a_1,a_2) ⊂ …) is only asserted.

The density argument on the slip needs continuity of the multilinear map E^n → \hat\Lambda^n E. This follows from the inequality being proved, so the ordering of the slip relative to the main text is slightly circular as drafted. It is harmless, since the e_J are orthonormal and the finite-dimensional case suffices.
Equation numbering is in flux: the slip renumbers e_J as (5), while on the previous page (5) was the norm inequality.

ideas.what: Hilbert-space exterior power \hat\Lambda^n E with inner product given by the Gram determinant, and Hilbert basis e_J indexed by n-element subsets
ideas.modern_name: Exterior power of a Hilbert space / antisymmetric (fermionic) Fock space component
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Grassmann; Hilbert-space version folklore by the 1930s–40s, e.g. in quantum field theory and Murray–von Neumann-era operator theory)
ideas.where_published: Exterior powers of Banach/Hilbert spaces and their use for Fredholm determinants appear in Grothendieck, 'La théorie de Fredholm', Bull. SMF 84 (1956); topological tensor products in 'Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires', Mem. AMS 16 (1955)

ideas.what: Gram determinant equals |det A|^2, and Hadamard's inequality proved by triangularization
ideas.where_published: Possibly used implicitly in the Fredholm determinant estimates of 'La théorie de Fredholm' (1956); unsure of an explicit statement

ideas.what: |det((a_i,b_j))| ≤ ∏||a_i|| ||b_i|| (Cauchy–Schwarz in \Lambda^n E), leading on the next page to ||u_1∧…∧u_n|| ≤ ∏||u_i||, i.e. norm-1 constants in the Hilbert case
ideas.modern_name: Contractivity of exterior powers of operators on Hilbert space; the basis of Fredholm/Carleman determinant estimates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fredholm, Hadamard, Carleman for determinant bounds; standard in Simon's 'Trace ideals')
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'La théorie de Fredholm' (1956) treats exterior powers of operators and Fredholm determinants

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook-level construction: the Hilbert exterior power, its orthonormal basis, and Hadamard's inequality with a standard proof. It is drafted as background for Grothendieck's Fredholm-theory work, whose substance was published in 1955–56. Its only interest is as a draft documenting how he set up the Hilbert case with constants equal to 1.
transcription_corrections: The slip inserts 'orthonormale' (or 'orthonormée') above 'base hilbertienne'; the reading 'pour toute partie J à n éléments … de I' is plausible.

After 'système orthonormal' the insertion is likely 'complet'. The struck lines mention E_0 being dense in E and its image in \hat\Lambda E under the multilinear map; the transcription's '[-... pour ... dense dans E ...-]' is a fair summary.
On this page the matrix is written 'AA*', not '{}^tA A^*' as in the previous page's transcription. A superscript-like mark before AA* may be a stray stroke.
'parallélotope' in the transcription is probably 'parallélépipède' in the hand (matching the previous page's transcription); illegible either way.
The second (b_j) entries in the corollary are written det(a_i,b_j) ≤ ∏_i ||a_i|| ||b_i||, with the 'Alors on a' clause partly illegible.
